problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x+2y,\,y(1)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method with step size $Δx=\frac{1}{4}.$ Fill in the empty box in the column for $Δy$ in the table below using this method. Do not round the answer.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ |  |  | {{field-1}} |

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3x-4y,\,y(1)=2
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method. What entry should be placed in the column for $Δy$ in the table below if the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2}?$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $$ | $$ | $\,?\,$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
First, because the initial condition is $y(1)=2,$ we fill $y=2$ into the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $$ | $$ |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =3x-4y \\  & =3\cdot 1-4\cdot 2 \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-5$ | $$ |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-5$ | $-\frac{5}{2}$ |
